rules.statement: In an Aspire AppHost, make a dependent resource wait on the API's readiness health check (`WithHttpHealthCheck` on the readiness endpoint plus `.WaitFor(api)`), not just on the process having started.
rules.why: Starting UIs alongside the API with no ordering lets them race it and fail. Gating on readiness removes that race reliably.
rules.check: Look for AppHost resources that call the API but have no `.WaitFor(...)`, or an API resource without `WithHttpHealthCheck` pointing at its readiness endpoint.

rules.statement: Keep the Aspire AppHost as its own sibling orchestration project that references the host, never nested inside the host project, and mark it `IsPackable=false` so it ships no artifact.
rules.why: The host must stay a single process. The AppHost is dev-only tooling, and keeping it unpackable means the pack, PublicAPI and provenance gates skip it.
rules.check: Look for Aspire `DistributedApplication` code inside a shipping host project, or an AppHost csproj that lacks `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>`.

rules.statement: Pin the `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` version under `msbuild-sdks` in global.json, and set `Aspire.Hosting.*` package versions centrally in Directory.Packages.props, moving them in lockstep.
rules.why: Central package management with lockstep versioning stops the SDK and the hosting packages drifting apart.
rules.check: Look for an Aspire SDK version written inline in the csproj `Sdk` attribute, or `Aspire.Hosting.*` PackageReferences that carry a `Version`.

rules.statement: When Aspire runs JavaScript resources from a shared pnpm workspace, turn off per-resource install (`WithPnpm(install: false)`) and install the workspace once, serially, from a single bootstrap script. Never add a per-app `pnpm install`.
rules.why: Two `pnpm install` runs at once against the workspace's shared, symlinked node_modules collide with ERR_PNPM_EBUSY and fail the dependent resource.
rules.check: Look for `WithPnpm()` without `install: false`, or for per-app `pnpm install` steps added to orchestration or repair code.

rules.statement: Pin local-dev endpoints whose ports are baked into redirect URIs, CORS origins or bootstrap documents to fixed ports, un-proxied (`IsProxied = false`), and do not let Aspire assign them dynamically.
rules.why: Seeded redirect URIs, CORS allowlists and the issuer, cookie and antiforgery binding assume those exact origins. A dynamic or host-rewriting proxy breaks them.
rules.check: Look for API or SPA endpoints in the AppHost with no explicit port, or with proxying left on, when other config hard-codes that origin.

rules.statement: Serve every local-dev browser surface over HTTPS with the ASP.NET Core development certificate (for example `WithHttpsDeveloperCertificate` for Vite resources), and register only `https://` dev redirect URIs and CORS origins.
rules.why: The browser can then trust one certificate across the whole stack, and the seeded redirect and CORS origins stay `https` only.
rules.check: Look for `http://` dev redirect URIs or CORS origins, or Vite resources that don't opt into the development certificate.

rules.statement: Keep backing services such as databases or caches in local-dev orchestration opt-in, so the stack's basic run has no hard requirement on those containers.
rules.why: The zero-setup SQLite/in-memory inner loop must keep working. Making containers mandatory breaks that promise.
rules.check: Look for AppHost changes that make a container resource required for the default run with no opt-in switch.

rules.statement: In local dev, get runtime bootstrap/config documents from the real host endpoint (for example through a dev-server proxy to the API origin) instead of shipping a static dev copy.
rules.why: Using the real runtime endpoint means local dev cannot drift from production.
rules.check: Look for checked-in static bootstrap or config JSON used only in dev, in place of proxying to the API.
